claims.claim: On 28 Nov 2022 a live stream reached 4.6 million views during the first half of Brazil v Switzerland
claims.note: Body: 4,6 milhões de visualizações às 13h28, durante o 1º tempo; article published 28 Nov 2022.

claims.claim: Poder360 called it his second straight YouTube live record, after Marília Mendonça
claims.note: Source: 'o 2º recorde consecutivo de live mais assistida do YouTube'; previous record held by Marília Mendonça.

claims.claim: CazéTV ranked first in Tubefilter's global subscriber chart for the second week running (2026)
claims.note: Source: 'is #1 ... for the second week in a row'.

claims.claim: Casimiro Miguel, known as Cazé, is a journalist and streamer
claims.note: Source: 'Casimiro Miguel, também conhecido como Cazé, é jornalista e streamer.'

claims.claim: Tubefilter calls him a Brazilian creator
claims.note: Source: 'the Brazilian creator (whose real name is Casimiro Miguel)'.

claims.claim: Born in Rio de Janeiro in October 1993, no day given; the article says it is the only source for birthplace and birth month
claims.note: Source explicitly: 'Casimiro nasceu no Rio de Janeiro, em outubro de 1993.' Only one source found; the body now says so.

claims.claim: He studied journalism at university without finishing the course
claims.note: Source: 'estudou jornalismo na faculdade, mas não chegou a concluir o curso'.

claims.claim: He opened his Twitch channel in September 2018
claims.note: Source: 'criou um canal na Twitch em setembro de 2018'.

claims.claim: He became widely known during the pandemic through reaction streams, playing FIFA and GTA
claims.note: Source: 'durante a pandemia', reactions, 'games como FIFA e GTA'.

claims.claim: 24 Jan 2022 stream of the Neymar documentary pre-premiere peaked at about 545,000 viewers; Canaltech reported it as a Brazilian Twitch record
claims.note: Source: 'nesta segunda-feira (24)', published 25/01/2022; 'cerca de 545 mil pessoas'; 'recorde da Twitch brasileira de maior transmissão geral'. The full date is inferred from the weekday and the publication date.

claims.claim: By early March 2022 Correio Braziliense reported YouTube wanted to host his lives, with more than 600,000 concurrent viewers
claims.note: Published 04/03/2022: 'mais de 600 mil telespectadores conectados simultaneamente'.

claims.claim: CazéTV was launched in November 2022 to cover the Qatar World Cup
claims.note: Source: 'lançada em novembro de 2022, durante a Copa do Mundo do Catar'.

claims.claim: The channel broadcast 22 matches in a traditional format with a narrator and commentators
claims.note: Source: 'transmitir 22 partidas do torneio'; 'formato tradicional de transmissão de futebol, com narrador e comentaristas'.

claims.claim: The Switzerland stream body says 4.6 million views, the subtitle says 4 million simultaneous accesses
claims.note: Subtitle: '4 milhões de acessos simultâneos'; body: '4,6 milhões de visualizações'.

claims.claim: CazéTV had 3.16 million subscribers and his personal channel 859,000 in the Poder360 article
claims.note: Source: '3,16 milhões de inscritos' and '859 mil'. No date beyond publication (28 Nov 2022).

claims.claim: GQ Brasil named him Homem do Ano in digital content in November 2022; Metropoles reported it on 3 November
claims.note: Source: 'quinta-feira (3/11)', Homem do Ano, Conteúdo Digital, GQ Brasil; article dated 03/11/2022.

claims.claim: He had also won iBest's Twitcher do Ano and eSports Brasil's Personalidade do Ano (no year given)
claims.note: Source names both awards; the 2021 year was removed from the article because the source does not date the wins.

claims.claim: Canaltech named him Streamer of the Year at its sixth awards, article of March 2023
claims.note: Source: 'streamer do ano no 6º Prêmio Canaltech', published 14/03/2023.

claims.claim: He told his mother he would work to retire his parents, and once thought he would not make it in life
claims.note: Source: 'Eu falei para a minha mãe...' and 'Tinha para mim que eu não ia dar certo na vida'. The earlier wording about streaming was corrected.

claims.claim: For the 2026 World Cup CazéTV again carried the matches on YouTube
claims.note: Source: 'broadcasting every match of the World Cup on YouTube'.

A Brazil v Japan knockout broadcast reached 21.1 million concurrent viewers

valueNote: Gives a dated timeline from Twitch to CazéTV, flags the Poder360 inconsistency, flags the single-source birthplace, and separates the 2026 subscriber figures by date and channel.
summary: All dated and numeric claims were checked against the opened sources. Birthplace and birth month rest on Canaltech alone, and the body now says so. Corrections made: removed an unsourced 3.5 million figure and its date, removed the year 2021 for the iBest and eSports Brasil awards, and corrected the quote about streaming to the source's wording.
